report:
Your “no” is probably too strong: the better answer is “yes, possibly, but not proven.” Monk’s pepper is *Vitex agnus-castus*/chasteberry. A randomized double-blind placebo-controlled BMJ trial over three cycles found agnus castus fruit extract improved PMS symptoms more than placebo (https://www.bmj.com/content/322/7279/134). A 2017 systematic review/meta-analysis found 13 of 14 controlled studies reported benefit, but warned most trials had high bias risk (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28237870/). A 2019 meta-analysis restricted to properly characterized products still found chasteberry more effective than placebo (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0965229919306053). NCCIH notes short-term use is generally well tolerated (https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/chasteberry).

So: it may reduce irritability, low mood, breast tenderness, bloating, or headache for some, especially standardized extracts, but product and study quality vary. Avoid in pregnancy and check interactions (hormonal therapies, dopamine-related drugs); seek care for severe PMS/PMDD.
